ca_certificate.description: Path to MikroTik's certificate authority file.

hosturl.description:
URL of the MikroTik router, default is TLS connection to REST.    
	* API: api[s]://host[:port]
		* api://router.local
		* apis://router.local:8729
	* REST: https://host
		* https://router.local
		* router.local
		* 127.0.0.1  


	export ROS_HOSTURL=router.local or export MIKROTIK_HOST=router.local

insecure.description: Whether to verify the SSL certificate or not.

username.description:
Username for the MikroTik WEB/Winbox.


	export ROS_USERNAME=admin or export MIKROTIK_USER=admin

___id___.description: Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

___path___.description: Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

admin_mac.description: Static MAC address of the bridge. This property only has effect when auto-mac is set to no.

ageing_time.description: How long a host's information will be kept in the bridge database.

arp_timeout.description: ARP timeout is time how long ARP record is kept in ARP table after no packets are received from IP. Value auto equals to the value of arp-timeout in IP/Settings, default is 30s. Can use postfix ms, s, M, h, d for milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days. If no postfix is set then seconds (s) is used.

auto_mac.description: Automatically select one MAC address of bridge ports as a bridge MAC address, bridge MAC will be chosen from the first added bridge port. After a device reboot, the bridge MAC can change depending on the port-number.

ether_type.description: This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

forward_delay.description: Time which is spent during the initialization phase of the bridge interface (i.e., after router startup or enabling the interface) in listening/learning state before the bridge will start functioning normally.

frame_types.description: Specifies allowed frame types on a bridge port. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

igmp_snooping.description: Enables multicast group and port learning to prevent multicast traffic from flooding all interfaces in a bridge.

ingress_filtering.description: Enables or disables VLAN ingress filtering, which checks if the ingress port is a member of the received VLAN ID in the bridge VLAN table. Should be used with frame-types to specify if the ingress traffic should be tagged or untagged. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

max_message_age.description: Changes the Max Age value in BPDU packets, which is transmitted by the root bridge. This property only has effect when protocol-mode is set to stp or rstp. Value: 6s..40s

mtu.description: The default bridge MTU value without any bridge ports added is 1500. The MTU value can be set manually, but it cannot exceed the bridge L2MTU or the lowest bridge port L2MTU. If a new bridge port is added with L2MTU which is smaller than the actual-mtu of the bridge (set by the mtu property), then manually set value will be ignored and the bridge will act as if mtu=auto is set.

priority.description: Bridge priority, used by STP to determine root bridge, used by MSTP to determine CIST and IST regional root bridge. This property has no effect when protocol-mode is set to none.

protocol_mode.description: Select Spanning tree protocol (STP) or Rapid spanning tree protocol (RSTP) to ensure a loop-free topology for any bridged LAN.

pvid.description: Port VLAN ID (pvid) specifies which VLAN the untagged ingress traffic is assigned to. It applies e.g. to frames sent from bridge IP and destined to a bridge port. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

transmit_hold_count.description: The Transmit Hold Count used by the Port Transmit state machine to limit transmission rate.

vlan_filtering.description: Globally enables or disables VLAN functionality for bridge.

___id___.description: Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

___path___.description: Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

auto_isolate.description: When enabled, prevents a port moving from discarding into forwarding state if no BPDUs are received from the neighboring bridge. The port will change into a forwarding state only when a BPDU is received. This property only has an effect when protocol-mode is set to rstp or mstp and edge is set to no.

bpdu_guard.description: This property has no effect when protocol-mode is set to none.

broadcast_flood.description: When enabled, bridge floods broadcast traffic to all bridge egress ports. When disabled, drops broadcast traffic on egress ports.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

edge.description: Set port as edge port or non-edge port, or enable edge discovery. Edge ports are connected to a LAN that has no other bridges attached.

edge_port.description: Whether port is an edge port or not.

edge_port_discovery.description: Whether port is set to automatically detect edge ports.

external_fdb_status.description: Whether registration table is used instead of forwarding data base.

fast_leave.description: Enables IGMP Fast leave feature on the port.

forwarding.description: Shows if the port is not blocked by (R/M)STP.

frame_types.description: Specifies allowed ingress frame types on a bridge port. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

horizon.description: Use split horizon bridging to prevent bridging loops. Set the same value for group of ports, to prevent them from sending data to ports with the same horizon value. Split horizon is a software feature that disables hardware offloading. This value is integer '0'..'429496729' or 'none'.

hw_offload_group.description: Switch chip used by the port.

ingress_filtering.description: Enables or disables VLAN ingress filtering, which checks if the ingress port is a member of the received VLAN ID in the bridge VLAN table. Should be used with frame-types to specify if the ingress traffic should be tagged or untagged. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

internal_path_cost.description: Path cost to the interface for MSTI0 inside a region. This property only has effect when protocol-mode is set to mstp.

learn.description: Changes MAC learning behaviour on a bridge port

learning.description: Shows whether the port is capable of learning MAC addresses.

multicast_router.description: Changes the state of a bridge port whether IGMP membership reports are going to be forwarded to this port.

path_cost.description: Path cost to the interface, used by STP to determine the "best" path, used by MSTP todetermine "best" path between regions. This property has no effect when protocol-mode is set to none.

point_to_point.description: Specifies if a bridge port is connected to a bridge using a point-to-point link for faster convergence in case of failure. This property has no effect when protocol-mode is set to none.

point_to_point_port.description: Whether the port is connected to a bridge port using full-duplex (true) or half-duplex (false).

port_number.description: Port number will be assigned in the order that ports got added to the bridge, but this is only true until reboot. After reboot internal numbering will be used.

priority.description: The priority of the interface, used by STP to determine the root port, used by MSTP to determine root port between regions.

pvid.description: ort VLAN ID (pvid) specifies which VLAN the untagged ingress traffic is assigned to. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

restricted_role.description: Enable the restricted role on a port, used by STP to forbid a port becoming a root port. This property only has effect when protocol-mode is set to mstp.

restricted_tcn.description: Disable topology change notification (TCN) sending on a port, used by STP to forbid network topology changes to propagate. This property only has effect when protocol-mode is set to mstp.

role.description: (R/M)STP algorithm assigned role of the port

sending_rstp.description: Whether the port is sending RSTP or MSTP BPDU types. A port will transit to STP type when RSTP/MSTP enabled port receives a STP BPDU

tag_stacking.description: Forces all packets to be treated as untagged packets. Packets on ingress port will be tagged with another VLAN tag regardless if a VLAN tag already exists, packets will be tagged with a VLAN ID that matches the pvid value and will use EtherType that is specified in ether-type. This property only has effect when vlan-filtering is set to yes.

trusted.description: When enabled, it allows to forward DHCP packets towards DHCP server through this port. Mainly used to limit unauthorized servers to provide malicious information for users. This property only has effect when dhcp-snooping is set to yes.

unknown_multicast_flood.description: When enabled, bridge floods unknown multicast traffic to all bridge egress ports.

unknown_unicast_flood.description: When enabled, bridge floods unknown unicast traffic to all bridge egress ports.

bridge.description: The bridge interface which the respective VLAN entry is intended for.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

tagged.description: Interface list with a VLAN tag adding action in egress. This setting accepts comma separated values. E.g. tagged=ether1,ether2.

untagged.description: Interface list with a VLAN tag removing action in egress. This setting accepts comma separated values. E.g. untagged=ether3,ether4

vlan_ids.description: The list of VLAN IDs for certain port configuration. This setting accepts VLAN ID range as well as comma separated values. E.g. vlan-ids=100-115,120,122,128-130.

add_default_route.description: Whether to install default route in routing table received from DHCP server.

address.description: IP address and netmask, which is assigned to DHCP Client from the Server.

default_route_distance.description: Distance of default route. Applicable if add-default-route is set to yes.

dhcp_options.description: Options that are sent to the DHCP server.

dhcp_server.description: The IP address of the DHCP server.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

expires_after.description: A time when the lease expires (specified by the DHCP server).

gateway.description: The IP address of the gateway which is assigned by DHCP server.

primary_dns.description: The IP address of the first DNS resolver, that was assigned by the DHCP server

secondary_dns.description: The IP address of the second DNS resolver, assigned by the DHCP server

use_peer_dns.description: Whether to accept the DNS settings advertised by DHCP Server (will override the settings put in the /ip dns submenu).

use_peer_ntp.description: Whether to accept the NTP settings advertised by DHCP Server (will override the settings put in the /system ntp client submenu).

address_pool.description: IP pool, from which to take IP addresses for the clients. If set to static-only, then only the clients that have a static lease (added in lease submenu) will be allowed.

authoritative.description: Option changes the way how a server responds to DHCP requests.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

lease_script.description: A script that will be executed after a lease is assigned or de-assigned.

lease_time.description: The time that a client may use the assigned address. The client will try to renew this address after half of this time and will request a new address after the time limit expires.

address.description: The IP address of the DHCP lease to be created.

address_list.description: Address list to which address will be added if lease is bound.

allow_dual_stack_queue.description: Creates a single simple queue entry for both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, uses the MAC address and DUID for identification.

block_access.description: Whether to block access for this DHCP client (true|false).

client_id.description: If specified, must match DHCP 'client identifier' option of the request.

dhcp_option_set.description: Add additional set of DHCP options.

dynamic.description: Whether the dhcp lease is static or dynamic. Dynamic leases are not guaranteed to continue to be assigned to that specific device. Defaults to false.

insert_queue_before.description: Specify where to place dynamic simple queue entries for static DCHP leases with rate-limit parameter set.

lease_time.description: Time that the client may use the address. If set to 0s lease will never expire.

mac_address.description: The MAC addreess of the DHCP lease to be created.

rate_limit.description: Adds a dynamic simple queue to limit IP's bandwidth to a specified rate. Requires the lease to be static.

server.description: Server name which serves this client.

use_src_mac.description: When this option is set server uses source MAC address instead of received CHADDR to assign address.

block.description: Creates a DHCP lease on the mikrotik device.

address.description: The network DHCP server(s) will lease addresses from.

caps_manager.description: A comma-separated list of IP addresses for one or more CAPsMAN system managers. DHCP Option 138 (capwap) will be used.

dhcp_option.description: Add additional DHCP options from the option list.

dhcp_option_set.description: Add an additional set of DHCP options.

dns_none.description: If set, then DHCP Server will not pass dynamic DNS servers configured on the router to the DHCP clients if no DNS Server in DNS-server is set.

dns_server.description: the DHCP client will use these as the default DNS servers. Two comma-separated DNS servers can be specified to be used by the DHCP client as primary and secondary DNS servers.

domain.description: The DHCP client will use this as the 'DNS domain' setting for the network adapter.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

gateway.description: The default gateway to be used by DHCP Client.

netmask.description: The actual network mask is to be used by the DHCP client. If set to '0' - netmask from network address will be used.

next_server.description: The IP address of the next server to use in bootstrap.

ntp_server.description: The DHCP client will use these as the default NTP servers. Two comma-separated NTP servers can be specified to be used by the DHCP client as primary and secondary NTP servers

wins_server.description: The Windows DHCP client will use these as the default WINS servers. Two comma-separated WINS servers can be specified to be used by the DHCP client as primary and secondary WINS servers

ttl.description: The ttl of the DNS record.

address.description: A single IP address or range of IPs to add to address list or DNS name. You can input for example, '192.168.0.0-192.168.1.255' and it will auto modify the typed entry to 192.168.0.0/23 on saving.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

list.description: Name for the address list of the added IP address.

timeout.description:
Time after address will be removed from address list. If timeout is not specified,
the address will be stored into the address list permanently.  
	> Please plan your work logic based on the fact that after the timeout    
	> the resource has been destroyed outside of Terraform.

___id___.description: Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

___path___.description: Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.

action.description: Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule

address_list_timeout.description: Time interval after which the address will be removed from the address list specified by address-list parameter. Used in conjunction with add-dst-to-address-list or add-src-to-address-list actions.

bytes.description: The total amount of bytes matched by the rule.

chain.description: Specifies to which chain rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

connection_bytes.description: Matches packets only if a given amount of bytes has been transfered through the particular connection.

connection_limit.description: Matches connections per address or address block after given value is reached. Should be used together with connection-state=new and/or with tcp-flags=syn because matcher is very resource intensive.

connection_mark.description: Matches packets marked via mangle facility with particular connection mark. If no-mark is set, rule will match any unmarked connection.

connection_nat_state.description: Can match connections that are srcnatted, dstnatted or both.

connection_rate.description: Connection Rate is a firewall matcher that allow to capture traffic based on present speed of the connection (0..4294967295).

connection_state.description: Interprets the connection tracking analysis data for a particular packet.

connection_type.description: Matches packets from related connections based on information from their connection tracking helpers.

content.description: Match packets that contain specified text.

dst_address.description: Matches packets which destination is equal to specified IP or falls into specified IP range.

dst_address_list.description: Matches destination address of a packet against user-defined address list.

dst_limit.description: Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded.

dst_port.description: List of destination port numbers or port number ranges.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

fragment.description: Matches fragmented packets. First (starting) fragment does not count. If connection tracking is enabled there will be no fragments as system automatically assembles every packet

hotspot.description: Matches packets received from HotSpot clients against various HotSpot matchers.

hw_offload.description: Whether or not rule is hardware offloaded

in_bridge_port.description: Actual interface the packet has entered the router if the incoming interface is a bridge. Works only if use-ip-firewall is enabled in bridge settings.

in_bridge_port_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as in-bridge-port.

in_interface.description: Interface the packet has entered the router.

in_interface_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as in-interface.

ingress_priority.description: Matches the priority of an ingress packet. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, or MPLS EXP bit.

ipsec_policy.description: Matches the policy used by IPsec. Value is written in the following format: direction, policy.

jump_target.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if action=jump.

limit.description: Matches packets up to a limited rate (packet rate or bit rate). A rule using this matcher will match until this limit is reached. Parameters are written in the following format: rate[/time],burst:mode.

log.description: Add a message to the system log.

log_prefix.description: Adds specified text at the beginning of every log message. Applicable if action=log or log=yes configured.

nth.description: Matches every nth packet: nth=2,1 rule will match every first packet of 2, hence, 50% of all the traffic that is matched by the rule

out_bridge_port.description: Actual interface the packet is leaving the router if the outgoing interface is a bridge. Works only if use-ip-firewall is enabled in bridge settings.

out_bridge_port_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as out-bridge-port.

out_interface.description: Interface the packet is leaving the router.

out_interface_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as out-interface.

packet_mark.description: Matches packets marked via mangle facility with particular packet mark. If no-mark is set, the rule will match any unmarked packet.

packet_size.description: Matches packets of specified size or size range in bytes.

packets.description: The total amount of packets matched by the rule.

per_connection_classifier.description: PCC matcher allows dividing traffic into equal streams with the ability to keep packets with a specific set of options in one particular stream.

place_before.description:
Before which position the rule will be inserted.  
	> Please check the effect of this option, as it does not work as you think!  
	> Best way to use in conjunction with a data source. See [example](../data-sources/firewall.md#example-usage).

port.description: Matches if any (source or destination) port matches the specified list of ports or port ranges. Applicable only if protocol is TCP or UDP

priority.description: Matches the packet's priority after a new priority has been set. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, MPLS EXP bit, or from the priority that has been set using the set-priority action.

protocol.description: Matches particular IP protocol specified by protocol name or number.

psd.description: Attempts to detect TCP and UDP scans. Parameters are in the following format WeightThreshold, DelayThreshold, LowPortWeight, HighPortWeight.

random.description: Matches packets randomly with a given probability.

reject_with.description: Specifies ICMP error to be sent back if the packet is rejected. Applicable if action=reject.

routing_mark.description: Matches packets marked by mangle facility with particular routing mark.

routing_table.description: Matches packets which destination address is resolved in specific a routing table.

src_address.description: Matches packets which source is equal to specified IP or falls into a specified IP range.

src_address_list.description: Matches source address of a packet against user-defined address list.

src_mac_address.description: Matches source MAC address of the packet.

src_port.description: List of source ports and ranges of source ports. Applicable only if a protocol is TCP or UDP.

tcp_mss.description: Matches TCP MSS value of an IP packet.

time.description: Allows to create a filter based on the packets' arrival time and date or, for locally generated packets, departure time and date.

tls_host.description: Allows matching HTTPS traffic based on TLS SNI hostname.

new_mss.description:
Sets a new MSS for a packet.  
	> Clampt-to-pmtu feature sets (DF) bit in the IP header to dynamically discover the PMTU of a path.  
	> Host sends all datagrams on that path with the DF bit set until receives ICMP.  
	> Destination Unreachable messages with a code meaning "fragmentation needed and DF set".    
	> Upon receipt of such a message, the source host reduces its assumed PMTU for the path.

chain.description: Specifies to which chain rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

connection_bytes.description: Matches packets only if a given amount of bytes has been transfered through the particular connection.

connection_limit.description: Matches connections per address or address block after given value is reached. Should be used together with connection-state=new and/or with tcp-flags=syn because matcher is very resource intensive.

connection_mark.description: Matches packets marked via mangle facility with particular connection mark. If no-mark is set, rule will match any unmarked connection.

connection_rate.description: Connection Rate is a firewall matcher that allow to capture traffic based on present speed of the connection (0..4294967295).

connection_type.description: Matches packets from related connections based on information from their connection tracking helpers.

content.description: Match packets that contain specified text.

dst_address.description: Matches packets which destination is equal to specified IP or falls into specified IP range.

dst_address_list.description: Matches destination address of a packet against user-defined address list.

dst_limit.description: Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded.

dst_port.description: List of destination port numbers or port number ranges.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

fragment.description: Matches fragmented packets. First (starting) fragment does not count. If connection tracking is enabled there will be no fragments as system automatically assembles every packet

hotspot.description: Matches packets received from HotSpot clients against various HotSpot matchers.

in_bridge_port.description: Actual interface the packet has entered the router if the incoming interface is a bridge. Works only if use-ip-firewall is enabled in bridge settings.

in_bridge_port_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as in-bridge-port.

in_interface.description: Interface the packet has entered the router.

in_interface_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as in-interface.

ingress_priority.description: Matches the priority of an ingress packet. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, or MPLS EXP bit.

ipsec_policy.description: Matches the policy used by IPsec. Value is written in the following format: direction, policy.

jump_target.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if action=jump.

limit.description: Matches packets up to a limited rate (packet rate or bit rate). A rule using this matcher will match until this limit is reached. Parameters are written in the following format: rate[/time],burst:mode.

log.description: Add a message to the system log.

log_prefix.description: Adds specified text at the beginning of every log message. Applicable if action=log or log=yes configured.

nth.description: Matches every nth packet: nth=2,1 rule will match every first packet of 2, hence, 50% of all the traffic that is matched by the rule

out_bridge_port.description: Actual interface the packet is leaving the router if the outgoing interface is a bridge. Works only if use-ip-firewall is enabled in bridge settings.

out_bridge_port_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as out-bridge-port.

out_interface.description: Interface the packet is leaving the router.

out_interface_list.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as out-interface.

packet_mark.description: Matches packets marked via mangle facility with particular packet mark. If no-mark is set, the rule will match any unmarked packet.

packet_size.description: Matches packets of specified size or size range in bytes.

packets.description: The total amount of packets matched by the rule.

per_connection_classifier.description: PCC matcher allows dividing traffic into equal streams with the ability to keep packets with a specific set of options in one particular stream.

place_before.description:
Before which position the rule will be inserted.  
	> Please check the effect of this option, as it does not work as you think!  
	> Best way to use in conjunction with a data source. See [example](../data-sources/firewall.md#example-usage).

port.description: Matches if any (source or destination) port matches the specified list of ports or port ranges. Applicable only if protocol is TCP or UDP

priority.description: Matches the packet's priority after a new priority has been set. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, MPLS EXP bit, or from the priority that has been set using the set-priority action.

protocol.description: Matches particular IP protocol specified by protocol name or number.

psd.description: Attempts to detect TCP and UDP scans. Parameters are in the following format WeightThreshold, DelayThreshold, LowPortWeight, HighPortWeight.

random.description: Matches packets randomly with a given probability.

routing_mark.description: Matches packets marked by mangle facility with particular routing mark.

same_not_by_dst.description: Specifies whether to take into account or not destination IP address when selecting a new source IP address. Applicable if action=same

src_address.description: Matches packets which source is equal to specified IP or falls into a specified IP range.

src_address_list.description: Matches source address of a packet against user-defined address list.

src_mac_address.description: Matches source MAC address of the packet.

src_port.description: List of source ports and ranges of source ports. Applicable only if a protocol is TCP or UDP.

tcp_mss.description: Matches TCP MSS value of an IP packet.

time.description: Allows to create a filter based on the packets' arrival time and date or, for locally generated packets, departure time and date.

to_addresses.description: Replace original address with specified one. Applicable if action is dst-nat, netmap, same, src-nat.

to_ports.description: Replace the original port with the specified one. Applicable if action is dst-nat, redirect, masquerade, netmap, same, src-nat.

allow_fast_path.description: Whether to allow FastPath processing. Must be disabled if IPsec tunneling is used.

clamp_tcp_mss.description: Controls whether to change MSS size for received TCP SYN packets. When enabled, a router will change the MSS size for received TCP SYN packets if the current MSS size exceeds the tunnel interface MTU (taking into account the TCP/IP overhead). The received encapsulated packet will still contain the original MSS, and only after decapsulation the MSS is changed.

dscp.description: Set dscp value in GRE header to a fixed value '0..63' or 'inherit' from dscp value taken from tunnelled traffic.

ipsec_secret.description: When secret is specified, router adds dynamic IPsec peer to remote-address with pre-shared key and policy (by default phase2 uses sha1/aes128cbc).

keepalive.description: Tunnel keepalive parameter sets the time interval in which the tunnel running flag will remain even if the remote end of tunnel goes down. If configured time,retries fail, interface running flag is removed. Parameters are written in following format: KeepaliveInterval,KeepaliveRetries where KeepaliveInterval is time interval and KeepaliveRetries - number of retry attempts. KeepaliveInterval is integer 0..4294967295

active.description: A flag indicates whether the route is elected as Active and eligible to be added to the FIB.

dhcp.description: A flag indicates whether the route was added by the DHCP service.

distance.description: Value used in route selection. Routes with smaller distance value are given preference.

dst_address.description: IP prefix of route, specifies destination addresses that this route can be used for.

dynamic.description: Configuration item created by software, not by management interface. It is not exported, and cannot be directly modified.

ecmp.description: A flag indicates whether the route is added as an Equal-Cost Multi-Path route in the FIB.

gateway.description: Array of IP addresses or interface names. Specifies which host or interface packets should be sent to (IP | interface | IP%interface | IP@table[, IP | string, [..]]).

hw_offloaded.description: Indicates whether the route is eligible to be hardware offloaded on supported hardware.

immediate_gw.description: Shows actual (resolved) gateway and interface that will be used for packet forwarding.

pref_src.description: Which of the local IP addresses to use for locally originated packets that are sent via this route. Value of this property has no effect on forwarded packets. If value of this property is set to IP address that is not local address of this router then the route will be inactive (in ROS v6, ROS v7 allows IP spoofing).

routing_table.description: Routing table this route belongs to.

scope.description: Used in nexthop resolution. Route can resolve nexthop only through routes that have scope less than or equal to the target-scope of this route.

target_scope.description: Used in nexthop resolution. This is the maximum value of scope for a route through which a nexthop of this route can be resolved.

interval.description: Interval between two script executions, if time interval is set to zero, the script is only executed at its start time, otherwise it is executed repeatedly at the time interval is specified.

on_event.description: Name of the script to execute. It must be presented at /system script.

policy.description:
List of applicable policies:
    * dude - Policy that grants rights to log in to dude server.  
    * ftp - Policy that grants full rights to log in remotely via FTP, to read/write/erase files and to transfer files from/to the router. Should be used together with read/write policies.  
    * password - Policy that grants rights to change the password.  
    * policy - Policy that grants user management rights. Should be used together with the write policy. Allows also to see global variables created by other users (requires also 'test' policy).  
    * read - Policy that grants read access to the router's configuration. All console commands that do not alter router's configuration are allowed. Doesn't affect FTP.  
    * reboot - Policy that allows rebooting the router.  
    * romon - Policy that grants rights to connect to RoMon server.  
    * sensitive - Policy that grants rights to change "hide sensitive" option, if this policy is disabled sensitive information is not displayed.  
    * sniff - Policy that grants rights to use packet sniffer tool.  
    * test - Policy that grants rights to run ping, traceroute, bandwidth-test, wireless scan, snooper, and other test commands.  
    * write - Policy that grants write access to the router's configuration, except for user management. This policy does not allow to read the configuration, so make sure to enable read policy as well.  
policy = ["ftp", "read", "write"]

run_count.description: This counter is incremented each time the script is executed.

start_date.description: Date of the first script execution.

start_time.description: Time of the first script execution. If scheduler item has start-time set to startup, it behaves as if start-time and start-date were set to time 3 seconds after console starts up. It means that all scripts having start-time is startup and interval is 0 will be executed once each time router boots. If the interval is set to value other than 0 scheduler will not run at startup.

Value auto equals to the value of arp-timeout in IP/Settings, default is 30s. Can use postfix ms, s, M, h, d for milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours or days. If no postfix is set then seconds (s) is used.

authentication.description: Authentication method to use for VRRP advertisement packets.

group_master.description: Allows combining multiple VRRP interfaces to maintain the same VRRP status within the group.

interval.description: VRRP update interval in seconds. Defines how often master sends advertisement packets.

on_backup.description: Script to execute when the node is switched to the backup state.

on_fail.description: Script to execute when the node fails.

on_master.description: Script to execute when the node is switched to master state.

password.description: Password required for authentication. Can be ignored if authentication is not used.

preemption_mode.description: Whether the master node always has the priority. When set to 'no' the backup node will not be elected to be a master until the current master fails, even if the backup node has higher priority than the current master. This setting is ignored if the owner router becomes available

priority.description: Priority of VRRP node used in Master election algorithm. A higher number means higher priority. '255' is reserved for the router that owns VR IP and '0' is reserved for the Master router to indicate that it is releasing responsibility.

remote_address.description: Specifies the remote address of the other VRRP router for syncing connection tracking. If not set, the system autodetects the remote address via VRRP. The remote address is used only if sync-connection-tracking=yes.Sync connection tracking uses UDP port 8275.

sync_connection_tracking.description: Synchronize connection tracking entries from Master to Backup device.

v3_protocol.description: A protocol that will be used by VRRPv3. Valid only if the version is 3.

vrid.description: Virtual Router identifier. Each Virtual router must have a unique id number.

allowed_address.description: List of IP (v4 or v6) addresses with CIDR masks from which incoming traffic for this peer is allowed and to which outgoing traffic for this peer is directed. The catch-all 0.0.0.0/0 may be specified for matching all IPv4 addresses, and ::/0 may be specified for matching all IPv6 addresses.

current_endpoint_address.description: The most recent source IP address of correctly authenticated packets from the peer.

current_endpoint_port.description: The most recent source IP port of correctly authenticated packets from the peer.

endpoint_address.description: An endpoint IP or hostname can be left blank to allow remote connection from any address.

endpoint_port.description: An endpoint port can be left blank to allow remote connection from any port.

last_handshake.description: Time in seconds after the last successful handshake.

persistent_keepalive.description: A seconds interval, between 1 and 65535 inclusive, of how often to send an authenticated empty packet to the peer for the purpose of keeping a stateful firewall or NAT mapping valid persistently. For example, if the interface very rarely sends traffic, but it might at anytime receive traffic from a peer, and it is behind NAT, the interface might benefit from having a persistent keepalive interval of 25 seconds.

preshared_key.description: A **base64** preshared key. Optional, and may be omitted. This option adds an additional layer of symmetric-key cryptography to be mixed into the already existing public-key cryptography, for post-quantum resistance.

public_key.description: The remote peer's calculated public key.

rx.description: The total amount of bytes received from the peer.

tx.description: The total amount of bytes transmitted to the peer.
